headline: 2 arrested as primary school headteacher dies after mugging in Dhaka
summary: Ronjila Parvin, headteacher of Bagbari Girls’ Government Primary School, died after falling from a rickshaw when muggers pulled her bag near the parliament complex.
details: Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) has arrested two people, including the prime suspect, over the killing of a primary school headteacher who died after a mugging incident in Dhaka.

The victim, Ronjila Parvin, was the headteacher of Bagbari Girls’ Government Primary School in Bogura. She had traveled to Dhaka with her husband to consult a doctor at the Ispahani Islamia Eye Institute and Hospital.

The incident occurred around 6:30 am yesterday morning near the South Plaza area of the parliament complex. Two muggers on a motorcycle approached from behind and pulled at her bag while she was in a rickshaw.
During the struggle, Ronjila fell from the rickshaw and suffered severe head injuries and a fractured spine. She was declared dead at Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital.
The victim's husband, Abdul Matin, witnessed the incident and later filed a murder case with the Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station against two unidentified muggers.
The arrestees have been identified as Poni, also known as Para Poni, the prime suspect, and one of his associates. RAB will hold a press briefing at its Bosila headquarters this afternoon.

headline: Dhaka to ban battery-powered rickshaws on main roads
summary: Authorities are targeting these vehicles to reduce traffic congestion and curb power theft, despite their popularity as a cheap transport option.
details: Battery-powered rickshaws are set to be banned from Dhaka's main roads to tackle growing traffic congestion and safety concerns.
The move comes as these vehicles are often linked to widespread power theft, as owners charge batteries using illegal connections.
Officials state that the uncontrolled growth of these rickshaws has contributed to frequent accidents and severe gridlocks on major thoroughfares.
Despite the ban, these vehicles remain popular among commuters due to their low cost and ability to navigate narrow lanes where larger vehicles cannot enter.
The government aims to streamline urban transport by removing unregulated vehicles from primary roads while exploring sustainable alternatives.
